decision_conditions: The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of the decision notice. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the approved plans, as set out in the attached schedule which forms part of this notice. 497-D-17497-D-02 REV A 497-D-15 REV B497-D-13 REV B497-D-12 REV B497-D-18497-D-04 REV A497-D-16497-D-03 REV A497-D-14 REV C Design & Access Statement497-D-01 (EXISTING LOCATION SITE PLAN & BLOCK PLAN)Environmental Statement - Energy StatementEnvironmental Statement - Be GreenFLOOD RISK ASSESSMENT & OUTLINE DRAINAGE STRATEGY (247052-6FRA-Rev 6)Heritage Statement & Archaeology Desk - Based Assessment	Outline Construction Logistics PlanConstruction Management PlanHIGHWAY IMPACT ASSESSMENT  Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

No development above ground level shall commence until details of external materials specification, samples and detailed drawings (at 1:20 and 1:5) including: brickwork (1m x 1m sample panel - inc. bond, joint and mortar); brick detailing such as soldier course to lintels (as a contemporary reinterpretation of the existing lintels); cladding/glazing to linking elements; roof junctions, ridge, eaves, parapets; window and door openings and installations including frame, panels, window bars (minimum reveal depth 1 brick / 215mm). The development shall be implemented and maintained thereafter in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance.

The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Construction Management Plan dated September 2024 unless otherwise agreed by the Local Planning Authority. This condition should be read in conjunction with the Informative also attached to the permission. Reason: To ensure construction does not lead to damage of the nearby public road network and to minimise disruption to the neighbouring properties.

No development above ground level shall commence until a high-quality landscaping detailed design and specification, including hard landscaping throughout the site, soft landscaping, garden area, front ramp and balustrade, boundary treatment and gates. The development shall be implemented and maintained thereafter in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance.

Prior to the occupation of the development full details of the specification of the air source heat pumps and PV panels, including the dimensions, make and model, and the sound pressure levels of the proposed units, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall be implemented and maintained thereafter in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To protect the residential amenity from noise and disturbance.

Prior to the occupation of the development a verification report demonstrating that the approved flood risk and SuDS measures specified in the Strategy (247052-6FRA - Rev 6, 29th October 2025) have been fully implemented shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The report shall include:A.	As built plans of the sustainable drainage systems including levels information.B.	Photographs of the completed sustainable drainage systems.C.	Any relevant certificates from the manufacturers/suppliers of any drainage features.REASON: To ensure the sustainable management of water, minimise flood risk, minimise discharge of surface water outside of the curtilage of the property and ensure that the drainage system will remain functional throughout the lifetime of the development in accordance with Policy CP28 of the Core Strategy, DMD 59-62, and Policies SI12 & SI13 of the London Plan and the NPPF.

No development or development shall take place until a stage 1 written scheme of investigation (WSI) has been submitted to and approved by the local planning authority in writing. For land that is included within the WSI, no development shall take place other than in accordance with the agreed WSI, and the programme and methodology of site evaluation and the nomination of a competent person(s) or organisation to undertake the agreed works. If heritage assets of archaeological interest are identified by stage 1 then for those parts of the site which have archaeological interest a stage 2 WSI shall be submitted to and approved by the local planning authority in writing. For land that is included within the stage 2 WSI, no development shall take place other than in accordance with the agreed stage 2 WSI which shall include:A.	The statement of significance and research objectives, the programme and methodology of site investigation and recording and the nomination of a competent person(s) or organisation to undertake the agreed works.B.	Where appropriate, details of a programme for delivering related positive public benefits.C.	The programme for post-investigation assessment and subsequent analysis, publication & dissemination and deposition of resulting material. This part of the condition shall not be discharged until these elements have been fulfilled in accordance with the programme set out in the stage 2 WSI.Reason: In the interests of preserving any archaeological remains at the site.

Prior to occupation an acoustic report written in line with the methodology in BS4142:2014+A1 2019, shall be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. The report must set out the sound level generated from the combined air source heat pumps and state the noise control measures to be employed to ensure the noise from the air source heat pumps does not exceed a level of 5dB below the typical measured background noise level measured as L(A)90 15 minutes during operational hours, at the façade of the nearest or most noise affected residential property.Reason: To protect the local amenity from noise and disturbance.

All Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) of net power of 37kW and up to and including 560kW used during the course of the demolition, site preparation and construction phases shall comply with the emission standards set out in chapter 7 of the GLA's supplementary planning guidance "Control of Dust and Emissions During Construction and Demolition" dated July 2014 (SPG), or subsequent guidance. Unless it complies with the standards set out in the SPG, no NRMM shall be on site, at any time, whether in use or not, without the prior written consent of the local planning authority. The developer shall keep an up to date list of all NRMM used during the demolition, site preparation and construction phases of the development on the online register at https://nrmm.london/Reasons: In the interests of good air quality.

The windows on the side elevations on the ground and first floor shall be obscurely glazed and fixed shut and shall not be altered without the approval in writing of the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To safeguard the privacy of the occupiers of neighbouring properties.

Prior to occupation, the development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved secure cycle store details as set out in drawing (ref: 497-D-17). The secure cycle store shall be retained and maintained as such for the lifetime of the development.Reason: To ensure the provision of cycle parking in accordance with Policy T6.1 of the London Plan (2021), the Council's adopted standards and London Cycling Design Standards Chapter 8.

Prior to occupation, the development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved refuse store details as set out in drawing (ref: 497-D-17). The refuse store shall be retained and maintained as such for the lifetime of the development.Reason: In order to facilitate efficient, safe and clean removal of household refuse, the location and accessibility of refuse storage plus to maintain safety on the Highway.
